takeaway: 2–3 Sentinel-1 scenes give usable erosion maps. Abstention removes false alarms but hides real erosion; triage + prioritized review recovers most of it with 10–20 % review effort. There is no automatic accuracy gain.
abstract: Sentinel-1 radar maps riverbank erosion through clouds, but a quick post-monsoon map has few comparable scenes: only 2–3 ascending scenes each November over our 12-km Jamuna reach (Kurigram). We reproduced the Freihardt & Frey (2023) threshold rule on Earth Engine σ⁰ and scored every subset of 1–8 post-monsoon scenes (121 maps per rule) against an independent Sentinel-2 reference, tuning on 2024 only. With the published thresholds, false erosion fell from 74 ha (1 scene) to 24 ha (3 scenes), and F1 rose from 0.56 to 0.71, reaching 0.82 with 8 scenes. Agreement + abstention (v1) cut false erosion below 3 ha. However, it abstained on 9–12 % of pixels holding 14–21 ha of real erosion, so it did not beat a tuned baseline. A pre-registered v2 sorts pixels into high-confidence / review / stable and ranks review patches using map-date SAR only. On an independent reach (Sirajganj–Kazipur), prioritized review beat random review in 11 of 12 pre-registered tests, often by small margins. v2 adds no automatic accuracy gain.
findings: Scene budget: published-rule false erosion 74 → 24 → 7.5 ha (k = 1 → 3 → 8); tuned-baseline F1 0.70 → 0.79 → 0.82.

v1 A+G: decided-pixel F1 0.85–0.90 with < 3 ha false erosion, but 14–21 ha of real erosion was abstained. Counting UNCERTAIN as non-erosion, it was no better than the tuned baseline (Kurigram and Sirajganj).
v2 at 20 % review (Kurigram k = 3, exploratory): 21.3 ha recovered vs 5.5 ha for random review. Independent Sirajganj: both criteria met in 11/12 tests; failed at k = 8 (local 2025).
No automatic gain: v2 high-confidence F1 = v1, below the tuned baseline in every test. Single-scene maps still fail (31 Jan: 104 ha false).
contributions: Erosion-map scene-budget benchmark (121 subsets × 7 rules) of the published Sentinel-1/GEE method against an independent Sentinel-2 reference.
Abstention reported with coverage and abstained-erosion area — no hidden pixels.
Three-class triage + map-date review ranking, pre-registered (md5 + timestamps) and tested on an independent reach.
Root-cause audit of a failing scene (inundated fields, three independent sources); open pipeline with all CSVs.
limitations: Sentinel-2 is an optical reference, not field truth. Sirajganj 2025 has only 12 ha of erosion, with 67 % agreement on erosion points.
The reviewer is simulated as an oracle, and the REVIEW class covers 184–1218 ha. In Sirajganj 2024, randomly reviewing v1 UNCERTAIN pixels was almost as good at 20 % effort.
Kurigram 2025 v2 numbers are exploratory. Only two reaches of one river were tested, and overlapping subsets are not independent samples.
Historical mapping only — no forecasting, no PINN.
exp_b: maps possible on 8 Nov, 20 Nov and 2 Dec 2025 reached F1 0.73, 0.76 and 0.79 (tuned baseline, full coverage). A+G reached 0.82–0.84 on decided pixels, but only 0.66–0.70 with UNCERTAIN counted as non-erosion. Against an 'as-of mid-December' reference, the tuned baseline scored 0.75–0.82.
root_cause: Root-cause audit: no processing error. NoData, alignment (0-px shift), radiometry, mosaics and thresholds were all checked. The dark 31 Jan 2026 patches are temporarily inundated fields, a median 584 m from the channel. Evidence: GEE σ⁰ −15.0 dB vs −8.2 dB on control fields; also dark in the R150 descending scene; Sentinel-2 shows 88–99 % water from 28 Jan to 12 Feb. The scene was kept in every experiment. Alone it gives 160 ha of false erosion (tuned T); 2-scene A+G maps that contain it average 1.6 ha.
